title: The support does not depend on the chosen geometric point
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $x\in X$, and let $\bar x,\bar x'$ be
geometric points of $X$ with image $x$. For every etale sheaf
$F$ on $X_{\Et}$ one has $F_{\bar x}=0$ if and only if
$F_{\bar x'}=0$; consequently the
support of $F$ is independent of the
chosen geometric point over each of its points.

proof.text: Write $\Omega,\Omega'$ for the algebraically closed fields of $\bar x,\bar x'$ [def-weil-geometric-point], which are extensions of $\kappa(x)$, and choose a separable closure $\kappa(x)^s$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. By [lem-exc-etale-embedding-extension-sepclosed], applied with $E=\kappa(x)^s$, $F=L=\kappa(x)$ and the given inclusions $\kappa(x)\to\Omega$ and $\kappa(x)\to\Omega'$ (every element of $\kappa(x)^s$ is algebraic and separable over $\kappa(x)$, so its minimal polynomial splits in the algebraically closed fields $\Omega,\Omega'$), there are $\kappa(x)$-embeddings $e:\kappa(x)^s\to\Omega$ and $e':\kappa(x)^s\to\Omega'$. Let $s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)^s\to X$ be the composite of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)^s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ with the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. Then $\bar x=s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(e)$ and $\bar x'=s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(e')$, and $\bar y=\operatorname{Spec}(e)$, $\bar y'=\operatorname{Spec}(e')$ are geometric points of $Y=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)^s$ (the morphism $s$ itself need not be a geometric point, since $\kappa(x)^s$ need not be algebraically closed).

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence through the displayed inverse-image formulas

proof.text: Put $G=s^{-1}F$ on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] applied to $f=s:Y\to X$ and the geometric points $\bar y$, $\bar y'$ of $Y$, whose image geometric points are $\bar x$ and $\bar x'$, there are isomorphisms $G_{\bar y}\cong F_{\bar x}$ and $G_{\bar y'}\cong F_{\bar x'}$. The ring $\kappa(x)^s$ is a strictly henselian local ring: its maximal ideal is $0$, so idempotents of $B/0B=B$ lift uniquely for every finite algebra $B$, and its residue field $\kappa(x)^s$ is separably closed [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. By [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] applied to $R=\kappa(x)^s$, $S=Y$ and the geometric points $\bar y$, $\bar y'$ over its closed point, the germ maps $G(Y)\to G_{\bar y}$ and $G(Y)\to G_{\bar y'}$ are isomorphisms. Hence $F_{\bar x}\cong G_{\bar y}\cong G(Y)\cong G_{\bar y'}\cong F_{\bar x'}$.

The isomorphism in Step 2 gives $F_{\bar x}=0$ if and only if $F_{\bar x'}=0$. By [def-kun-support], membership of $x$ in the support is defined by nonvanishing of a geometric stalk over $x$, so the support is independent of the chosen geometric point.
